ethics_check.title: Ethics Approval Check
ethics_check.summary_text: All papers that appeared to involve live data collection contained an ethics approval statement.

table.text: UK Biobank has obtained research ethics approval from the North West Multicentre Research Ethics Committees (REC reference 11/NW/0382) and obtained written informed consent from all participants prior to the study.
Second, most participants were of European ancestry, and ancestry-specific estimates in smaller groups should be interpreted cautiously.
Participants were assigned to five genetic inferred ancestry populations: (African: AFR, Admixed American: AMR, East Asian: EAS, European: EUR, South Asian: SAS).
UK Biobank participants were then projected onto this PC space and assigned genetically inferred ancestry by maximum probability.
We therefore excluded all 4,826 EUR participants assigned to batch 7, and applied this step to all non-EUR populations.
AFR, AMR, EAS, and SAS participants were not partitioned and were used as external evaluation sets, separately and as a pooled non-EUR group.
Validation participants were not used for protein screening, base-learner fitting, and hyperparameter selection.

ethics_check.report:
Based on the following text, we would expect an ethics approval statement, and it was present:

> Second, most participants were of European ancestry, and ancestry-specific estimates in smaller groups should be interpreted cautiously.

> Participants were assigned to five genetic inferred ancestry populations: (African: AFR, Admixed American: AMR, East Asian: EAS, European: EUR, South Asian: SAS).

> UK Biobank participants were then projected onto this PC space and assigned genetically inferred ancestry by maximum probability.

> We therefore excluded all 4,826 EUR participants assigned to batch 7, and applied this step to all non-EUR populations.

> AFR, AMR, EAS, and SAS participants were not partitioned and were used as external evaluation sets, separately and as a pooled non-EUR group.

> Validation participants were not used for protein screening, base-learner fitting, and hyperparameter selection.

Ethics approval statement:

> UK Biobank has obtained research ethics approval from the North West Multicentre Research Ethics Committees (REC reference 11/NW/0382) and obtained written informed consent from all participants prior to the study.

power.title: Power Analysis Check
report: No power analyses were detected.

::: {.callout-tip title="Learn More" collapse="true"}

Power analyses need to contain the following information to be interpretable: the type of power analysis, the statistical test, the software used, sample size, critical alpha criterion, power level, effect size, and an effect size metric. In addition, it is recommended to make sure the power analysis is reproducible (by sharing the code, or a screenshot, of the power analysis), and to provide good arguments for why the study was designed to detect an effect of this size.

For an a-priori power analysis, where the sample size is determined, reporting all information would look like:

> An a priori power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that for a Cohen's d = 0.5, an alpha level of 0.05, and a desired power level of 80% required at least 64 participants in each group.

For a sensitivity power analysis, this sentence would look like:

> A sensitivity power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that with 64 participants in each group, and an alpha level of 0.05, a desired power level of 80% was reached for an effect size of d = 0.5.

:::

#### Files that do not belong in the repository

We left out 9 files that software creates by itself, not the authors: operating system (9). They hold nothing a reader can use, but they clutter the repository, and software can mistake them for real files (for example a `._` copy of a `.csv` for data).

*Remove these:* *Operating system* files: macOS adds a `__MACOSX` folder and a `._` copy of every file it puts in a zip, and `.DS_Store` files to folders; Windows adds `Thumbs.db` and `desktop.ini`. On a Mac, create zips from the command line with `zip -r -X`, or remove them afterwards with `zip -d archive.zip "__MACOSX/*" "*.DS_Store"`. *RStudio session files* (`.Rproj.user/`) hold open tabs and unsaved edits; *R history* (`.Rhistory`) lists the commands typed in a session and can hold file paths and passwords; *Jupyter checkpoints* (`.ipynb_checkpoints/`) are automatic copies of notebooks; *compiled Python files* (`__pycache__/`, `.pyc`) are recreated when the code runs; *open-document lock files* (`~$...docx`, `.~lock...#`) are left while a document is open; *editor backups* (`file~`, `.bak`, `.swp`) and *temporary files* (`.tmp`, `.temp`) are copies a program made by itself.

*Keep only on purpose:* *version control* folders (`.git`, `.svn`, `.hg`) hold the project's history, which can include earlier versions of files and data that was later removed; *editor settings* (`.idea`, `.vscode`) can hold paths on your own computer. A `.gitignore` based on GitHub's templates (https://github.com/github/gitignore) keeps them out of a repository.

summary_table.ethics_statements: UK Biobank has obtained research ethics approval from the North West Multicentre Research Ethics Committees (REC reference 11/NW/0382) and obtained written informed consent from all participants prior to the study.
live_data_statements: Second, most participants were of European ancestry, and ancestry-specific estimates in smaller groups should be interpreted cautiously.
Participants were assigned to five genetic inferred ancestry populations: (African: AFR, Admixed American: AMR, East Asian: EAS, European: EUR, South Asian: SAS).
UK Biobank participants were then projected onto this PC space and assigned genetically inferred ancestry by maximum probability.
We therefore excluded all 4,826 EUR participants assigned to batch 7, and applied this step to all non-EUR populations.
AFR, AMR, EAS, and SAS participants were not partitioned and were used as external evaluation sets, separately and as a pooled non-EUR group.
Validation participants were not used for protein screening, base-learner fitting, and hyperparameter selection.

**`setwd()` in the code**
**26 scripts call `setwd()`.** This is bad practice: it hardcodes where the code must run (often an absolute path on the author's own machine) and breaks the moment the code is run anywhere else. To run the code we replaced these calls with a statement that does nothing. Any such script that then ran is **reproducible only after ignoring a `setwd()` that should not have been in the code and needs to be fixed**.
